title: NCLT Allahabad: Written Loan Agreement Not Required to Admit Noida Firm Into Insolvency
case_name: Jyoti Kumar Arya (HUF) and Vineet Gunwani v. Megma RFID and Labels Private Limited
card_summary: The NCLT's Allahabad bench admitted an insolvency petition against Megma RFID and Labels Private Limited, a Noida-based RFID label maker, filed by two individual financial creditors. It held that the absence of a written loan agreement does not bar proof of financial debt once disbursement and default are shown. The process began on 26 October 2026, with claims due by 13 November 2026.
card_tip: Lenders who advanced money without a formal loan deed can still found a Section 7 petition on bank records and admissions; borrowers cannot treat an informal loan as undocumented and therefore unenforceable.
verification_notes: Confirmed via two independent reports (Taxscan, TaxGuru) of the same NCLT Allahabad order, consistent with Oquilia's report of the IBBI public announcement giving the 26 October 2026 admission date and 13 November 2026 claims deadline. Full judgment text not independently read; reported debt figure (Rs 1.71 crore) taken from Taxscan only.
